title: U.S. House · North Dakota At-Large

context.text: Incumbent Julie Fedorchak (R) defeated Alex Balazs 72.8%-27.0% in the June 9, 2026 Republican primary. Trygve Hammer won the Democratic primary essentially unopposed with 99.8% of the vote after Vern Thompson withdrew.

summary.text: Julie Fedorchak is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election to North Dakota's at-large House seat. A former North Dakota Public Service Commissioner, she serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee and has focused her time in office on energy production, agriculture and reducing federal spending.

background.text: Earned a B.A. in journalism from the University of North Dakota in 1991; began her career as a communications and media relations specialist.
Served as a spokesperson for Gov. Ed Schafer (R) from 1995 to 2000, and became North Dakota state director for U.S. Sen. John Hoeven (R) in 2011.
Volunteered as president of the National Association of Regulatory Utility Commissioners (NARUC) and president of the Organization of MISO States (OMS).

priorities.text: Says she is focused on energy affordability, reliability, sustainability and security, and wants to expand domestic energy production and lower costs.
Says she supports balancing the federal budget and rooting out wasteful spending, citing the scale of the national debt.
Says agriculture is the backbone of North Dakota's economy and supports improving the Farm Bill, strengthening crop insurance, and reducing regulations on farmers and ranchers.

positions.summary: In a September 2026 statement, welcomed the EPA's repeal of the power plant greenhouse gas rule known as Clean Power Plan 2.0 and criticized closing power plants early.
positions.quote: Prematurely closing power plants at a time when power demand is surging is irresponsible and reckless.

positions.summary: In a January 2026 statement explaining her vote against a discharge petition, said extending the enhanced Affordable Care Act premium tax credits would not achieve long-term goals and that she supports a glide path off the current program.
positions.quote: Extending the enhanced premium subsidies—a temporary program that Democrats created to expire—will not achieve these long-term goals

positions.summary: In a June 2026 statement supporting the Secure America Act, which funds ICE and Border Patrol through fiscal year 2029, said enforcement agents need more resources.
positions.quote: securing the border requires more than a return to enforcing the law—it requires giving the men and women on the front lines the resources they need to do their jobs.

positions.summary: In a March 2026 press release on the Iran strikes, her office stated the President has authority to take military action without prior congressional approval.
positions.quote: Under Article II of the U.S. Constitution, the President has constitutional authority to take military action to protect U.S. national interests without prior congressional approval, especially in response to imminent threats.

record.text: Sits on the House Energy and Commerce Committee, including the Communications and Technology, Energy, and Environment subcommittees, in the 119th Congress.

candidates.name: Trygve Hammer
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 9, 2026 Democratic primary with 99.8% of the vote after Vern Thompson withdrew; previously the Democratic nominee for this seat in 2024.

summary.text: Trygve Hammer is the Democratic nominee for North Dakota's at-large House seat, a Marine Corps veteran and former airline pilot who was also the Democratic nominee for the seat in 2024.

background.text: Served in the U.S. Marine Corps Reserve from 1990 to 2010, including as a helicopter pilot, forward air controller, military attaché at the U.S. Embassy in Rome, and instructor.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the U.S. Naval Academy in 1990.
Worked as an airline pilot, defense contractor and security consultant.

priorities.text: During his 2024 campaign for this seat, his website listed lowering prescription drug prices, protecting Social Security benefits, and support for rural schools and communities among his priorities.

positions.summary: In his 2026 Ballotpedia survey, calls for a tax code that asks as much of billionaires as it does of paychecks.
positions.quote: a tax code that asks as much of billionaires as it does of paychecks

positions.summary: In his 2026 Ballotpedia survey, says Congress must vote before U.S. forces are sent into combat.
positions.quote: Congress must vote before we send Americans into combat

positions.summary: In his 2026 Ballotpedia survey, lists restoring premium tax credits and protecting Medicaid as part of his health care priorities.
positions.quote: That means keeping rural hospitals open, restoring premium tax credits, and protecting Medicaid and Social Security.

candidates.researchNotes: Hammer has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey and no 2026 campaign website content was located; priorities and positions above are drawn from his 2024 campaign website, as quoted by Ballotpedia, and may not reflect any changes for 2026.
